hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
hook.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
hook.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
alternates.sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
alternates.line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
alternates.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
alternates.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
alternates.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
alternates.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
alternates.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.for_you: You are standing at a crossroads where everything is shifting at once, and the fear of how it will turn out is making the next step feel impossible. The work in front of you is yours to do, and the result is not yours to hold.
verse.try_today: Do one small task at work without checking how it will change your future.
verse.scene_line: You are on the battlefield of your own life, with the future waiting and the past behind you.
asks: How do I separate my effort from the result?
What if the work I do does not change anything?
How do I act when the outcome feels too big?

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Hanuman weighs fighting the guards against quietly reaching Sita first.
verse.sanskrit: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते। कश्च निःसंशयं कार्यं कुर्यात् प्राज्ञः ससंशयम्॥
verse.line: Don't turn a sure thing into a gamble. Do the certain part first.
verse.translation: Battles are uncertain, and I don't like a gamble. What wise person would turn a sure task into an unsure one?
verse.why: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.

prasang.title: How Hanuman spoke to Sita
prasang.summary: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.
prasang.story_hook: He had found her at last, and now the problem was how to speak without making her scream.
prasang.lesson: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.

verse.meaning: Hanuman has found Sita in the grove, and she is terrified of this monkey. He must decide whether to fight the guards and risk her life, or to speak gently and win her trust. He chooses the quiet path. He speaks in ordinary words, not the high language of the court. He starts by praising Ram, because that is the sure way to reach her heart. He knows that a fight is uncertain, but a gentle word is certain. He sings Ram's story from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time.
verse.for_you: You are standing at a crossroads, and every path looks like a gamble. You want to choose the sure thing, the one step that will not lose what you have found. Let your first move be the one that builds trust, not the one that proves a point.
verse.try_today: Notice the one small action that builds trust before it builds a case.
verse.scene_line: You are at the tree, and the first word must be gentle.
asks: Which path feels certain to me right now?
How do I tell the sure move from the proud one?
What is the quiet song I can sing today?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from the section on steadfastness. Imagine a person walking a path. People shout praise or blame from the roadside. Money appears or disappears. Death could come today or years from now. Through all of this, the steadfast person does not move a step from the right path.
verse.for_you: Your work is yours to do. The results are not yours to hold. Let the noise of what comes next stay outside your door. The path is clear right now. Take the next step and keep going.
verse.try_today: Focus on the one task in front of you without checking the outcome.
verse.scene_line: You are on a path where the noise of others cannot reach you.
asks: How do I know the right path when everything is changing?
What if my work never brings the results I hoped for?
Can I stay steady when the people around me are so loud?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति । धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
verse.line: Not begging for gain, not grieving loss: a steady mind stays cool and full.
verse.translation: He does not pray for gain, nor grieve over loss. The steady one's cool mind is filled as if with nectar.
verse.why: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka in the final verses of the text, describing the mind of the wise. He says the calm person does not beg for gain and does not grieve over loss. Their mind stays cool and full, as if filled with nectar. This is not about running from a busy life or chasing a quiet place. It is about holding the ordinary moments without letting the swings of outcome shake the ground under them.
verse.for_you: You are facing a lot of change at once and wondering if you could stay in your job or leave. The energy is there but it is caught in doubt. This verse suggests that the steadiness you need is not found in a new title or a different door.
verse.try_today: Notice one task at work and do it fully, letting the outcome stay separate.

verse.speaker: Medhavin
verse.setting: A young man named Medhavin urges his father not to keep postponing what truly matters.
verse.sanskrit: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verse.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verse.translation: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
verse.why: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
verse.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.

prasang.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
prasang.summary: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
prasang.lesson: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.

verse.meaning: A young man named Medhavin speaks to his father, who is still resting while the world moves on. The father speaks of study and ritual, but Medhavin tells him that death does not wait to see if your work is finished. The verse says to do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. It does not ask for endless work. It asks you to finish the certain part first, before the day slips away.
verse.for_you: You are standing at the edge of a big change and the waiting is eating your time. The doubt you feel is not a sign to pause. It is the cost of moving. Do the one thing you are sure of right now, and let the rest wait its turn.
verse.try_today: Write down the one task you are certain of and do it before the day ends.
verse.scene_line: You are the father in the story, and the day is already slipping past your window.
asks: What is the one certain task I can finish today?
How do I stop the waiting from becoming the whole day?

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: Ram wants to act now, but the rains have closed every road; Lakshman counsels waiting.
verse.sanskrit: शरत्कालं प्रतीक्षस्व प्रावृटकालोऽयमागतः। ततः सराष्ट्र सगणं रावणं तं वधिष्यसि॥
verse.line: The rains are here. Wait for autumn. Some seasons are for waiting, not fighting.
verse.translation: The rainy season has come; wait for autumn. Then you will defeat Ravana with his kingdom and his allies.
verse.why: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.

prasang.title: Waiting out the monsoon
prasang.summary: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.
prasang.story_hook: The rains came, and with them four months in which nothing at all could be done.
prasang.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.

verse.meaning: Ram is burning with grief and wants to march on Ravana right now, but the rains have flooded every road. Lakshman tells him the rainy season has come, and they must wait for autumn. Some seasons are for waiting, not fighting. Ram agrees to wait, and he stops grieving long enough to give Sugriva the time he needs.
verse.for_you: You are in a season of waiting too. The roads are closed. Do not turn a sure thing into a gamble by rushing into a change you cannot control. Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verse.try_today: Do the one certain task that is waiting for you today.
verse.scene_line: You are on a mountain, waiting for the rains to clear the road.
asks: How do I know if I am waiting or just delaying?
What is the one task I can do today?

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.line: When 'I still have to do this' burns you up inside, only a rain of calm brings relief.
verse.translation: For one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?
verse.why: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka in the final chapter of the Ashtavakra Gita, where he paints the life of the wise. He says that for the one whose heart is scorched by the blazing sun of 'things I must do', where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm? The verse tells us that calm is not a prize to be chased or a place to be reached. It is simply the way you hold ordinary life when the pressure of duty burns inside you.
verse.for_you: The pressure to manage every change at once is the blazing sun inside you. You are trying to secure the future before it arrives. Calm is not the absence of change. It is the cooling rain on the roof of your ordinary day, right where you are.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you stop checking what is next.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own city, under the sun of 'things I must do', waiting for the rain.
asks: Can the work be the work without my fear?
Where is the roof over my ordinary day?

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.setting: Nachiketa has refused wealth and long life; Yama begins teaching.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः । श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥
verse.line: The good and the pleasant both knock. The wise choose the good; the foolish grab the pleasant.
verse.translation: The good and the pleasant both come to a person. The wise one examines them and tells them apart. The wise chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull chooses the pleasant, for getting and keeping.
verse.why: Every day offers a choice between what feels good and what is good.

prasang.title: The good and the pleasant
prasang.summary: Yama praises Nachiketa for choosing the good over the pleasant. He explains that both come to every person, and the wise tell them apart, while the foolish choose what is pleasant and lose their way.
prasang.lesson: Every day offers a choice between what feels good and what is good.

verse.meaning: Yama, the god of death, speaks to Nachiketa after the boy refuses every worldly gift. He tells him that both what is pleasant and what is good will come to a person. The wise examine them and tell them apart, and they choose the good. The dull person grabs what is pleasant, wanting only to get and keep it.
verse.for_you: You are standing at a moment where many doors are opening at once, and each one promises a different kind of relief. The pleasant ones promise an easy exit, a quick win, or a way to stop feeling anxious.
verse.try_today: Notice which choice feels like an escape and which one asks you to stay.
verse.scene_line: You are at the threshold where two visitors knock, and you could tell them apart.
asks: What feels pleasant about staying in my job right now?
What does the good choice actually look like for me?
How do I know I am not just choosing what is easy?

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: In the forest, Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira. She tells him that waiting on fate is no plan for life. She says that if a person thinks, 'I keep working and still don't succeed,' that is no reason to despair. Every attempt can end two ways, in success or in failure. The only outcome that is certain is the one that comes from doing nothing at all.
verse.for_you: You are watching everything change at once. Do right for its own sake, then work as if the outcome depends entirely on you.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment you think effort is wasted, and choose to act anyway.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own forest, and the only certain outcome is the one that comes from waiting.
asks: How do I act when the result feels impossible?
How do I tell effort from pointless waiting?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
verse.line: The one who stays the same in pain and pleasure, undisturbed by either, is ready for real freedom.
verse.translation: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Steadiness is not numbness or hiding what you feel.

matched.label: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where grief has stopped him in his tracks. He tells Arjuna that the part of him which is never born and never dies is untouched by sorrow or joy. The steady person, he says, is the one who is not disturbed by either pain or pleasure, and this evenness is what makes a person ready for real freedom. The teaching is that your true nature outlasts every loss and every passing ache.
verse.for_you: You are facing a season where everything is shifting at once, and the question of staying or leaving is heavy. The teaching says that the part of you which is steady does not need to stop the storm. It only needs to remain even while the storm passes.
verse.scene_line: You are standing where the army waits, and the question is whether to move forward or turn back.
asks: How do I stay even when everything around me is shifting?
How do I know if I am choosing the good or just the easy way?

verse.speaker: Shiva
verse.setting: Shiva explains to his devotee Bhringi what makes a 'great doer'.
verse.sanskrit: यथार्थकाले मतिमानसंसक्तमना मुनिः । कार्यानुरूपवृत्तस्थो महाकर्ता स उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Act at the right time, do what the task needs, and don't cling. That is a great doer.
verse.translation: The thoughtful one who acts at the right time, with a mind unattached, doing what the task requires: that one is called a great doer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.meaning: Shiva tells his devotee Bhringi that a great doer acts at the right time and does what the task requires, but does not cling to the outcome. The idea is to work fully, enjoy fully, and let go fully. This anchors the mind inside so the work itself does not wear you out.
verse.for_you: Your life is changing at once and you are anxious about how it will turn out. This is the text's stuck and not starting.
verse.try_today: Pick one small task at work and do it without checking the result.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of a task, feeling the pull of everything else.
asks: What is the one task I can do fully right now?
How do I let go of the outcome while I work?
What does acting at the right time look like for me?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verse.sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
verse.line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
verse.translation: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
verse.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is asking Krishna why he must fight at all, if wisdom is the higher path. Krishna answers that no one can stop acting. The body moves whether the mind wants it or not. To sit still and think you are above it is only self-deception. Doing your own work is better than standing still. Even keeping the body alive needs action. So do the task that is yours.
verse.for_you: You are standing at the edge of a change you chose, but doubt is making the starting line feel like a wall. The texts say doing nothing is still a choice, and that choice is costing you the energy you could move.
verse.try_today: Pick one task at work and finish the first step of it before you check anything else.
verse.scene_line: You are Arjuna on the field, and the only action is the one you choose to take.
asks: How do I know if I am acting or just running away?
What is the smallest action that counts as doing my work?

story.title: Waiting out the monsoon
story.story_hook: The rains came, and with them four months in which nothing at all could be done.
story.summary: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.
story.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.

matched.label: Should I quit my job or stay

anchor.speaker: Ram
anchor.setting: Sugriva is enjoying his new kingdom and has not begun the search; Ram chooses to give him time.
anchor.sanskrit: स्वयमेव हि विश्रम्य ज्ञात्वा कालमुपागतम्। उपकारं च सुग्रीवो वेत्स्यते नात्र संशयः॥
anchor.line: Give people time. Once rested, a good friend remembers what they owe.
anchor.translation: Once he has rested, Sugriva will see for himself that the time has come and remember the help he received. I have no doubt.
anchor.why: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.
anchor.misuse: Patience with a friend has limits; when it runs out, Ram sends Lakshman (4.30).

prasang.title: Waiting out the monsoon
prasang.summary: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.
prasang.story_hook: The rains came, and with them four months in which nothing at all could be done.
prasang.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.

story.hook_title: Ram had to sit out four months of rain before he could look for Sita
story.teaser: Ram had to sit out four months of rain before he could look for Sita
story.for_you: You have set everything in motion, and now you are waiting to see what lands. You can rest in this pause without letting the doubt eat the ground you have already tilled. Let the waiting be a season, not a surrender.
asks: How do I know when the waiting is done and the work begins again?

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call stuck and not starting, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.core_struggle: Everything in my life is changing at once
understanding.mirror: Everything in my life is changing at once
understanding.insight: Doubt is spending the energy you would use to begin.

queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Doubt and delay feed each other; waiting to feel ready keeps us stuck, and the unacted-on decision weighs more than the work.
queries.steady: No effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and do the next right thing; act without waiting for certainty, and keep at it day by day.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
verse.line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
verse.translation: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, then this very moment you will be happy, at peace and free of bondage.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free. The boy answers at once. He says set the body apart from yourself, rest as the awareness that watches it, and right now you are already happy, calm and free. The idea is simple. You are not your roles, your work, or your worries. You are the awareness that sees them. Freedom is not a place to reach. It is the way you see yourself in this very moment.
verse.for_you: You are standing at a crossroads where everything is shifting, and the mind is telling you that you could choose the right path to be safe. Ashtavakra says the choice itself is not the problem. You are the awareness that watches the choices, not the choices themselves.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you feel the pressure to choose and do nothing but watch it.
verse.scene_line: You are Janaka asking the sage how to be free, and the answer is already in the room.
asks: How do I rest as awareness when my life is changing so fast?
What does it mean to set my body apart from myself?
Can I be free while I am still working and making choices?

verse.speaker: Shakayanya
verse.sanskrit: मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः । बन्धाय विषयासक्तं मुक्त्यै निर्विषयं स्मृतमिति ॥
verse.line: The mind alone binds or frees us: hooked on things, it binds; free of them, it liberates.
verse.translation: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and of liberation for human beings: attached to objects, it binds; free of objects, it liberates.
verse.why: Tend your mind; it decides whether you feel trapped or free.

prasang.title: The mind is your world
prasang.summary: The sage's verses on the mind: it is the world we live in, we become what it dwells on, and it alone binds or frees us depending on what it clings to.
prasang.lesson: Tend your mind; it decides whether you feel trapped or free.

verse.for_you: No effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verse.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
verse.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
verse.translation: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
verse.why: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

prasang.title: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

verse.meaning: Krishna is explaining the difference between the active world and the silent self. He tells Arjuna that the sky is vast and open, and nothing that moves through it, clouds, birds, wind, can leave a mark on it. In the same way, the true self is present inside every living body, but it remains completely untouched by the actions and changes that happen around it.
verse.for_you: You are standing at a point where everything is shifting at once, and your body feels the weight of every choice. But the part of you that is watching this change is not the thing that is changing. It is the sky, and it is clean.
verse.try_today: Notice when the body feels heavy, and let the watching part of you rest like the sky.
verse.scene_line: You are the sky in which every change passes, and nothing stains you.
asks: How do I rest as the sky while everything changes?
Can I feel the self untouched by the job I fear losing?
What does it mean to see the same presence in my own fear?

verse.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verse.setting: Verses on knowing the self, continued.
verse.sanskrit: इहैव सन्तोऽथ विद्मस्तद्वयं न चेदवेदिर्महती विनष्टिः । ये तद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्त्यथेतरे दुःखमेवापियन्ति ॥
verse.line: While we are still here, let us know it. Not knowing it is the great loss.
verse.translation: While we are still here, we may know it. If we do not, great is the loss. Those who know it become immortal; the rest go only to sorrow.
verse.why: You become what you desire and do; know what matters while you are here.

prasang.title: Yajnavalkya on desire and death
prasang.summary: Yajnavalkya explains what happens at death with images of a caterpillar and a goldsmith. A person becomes what they desire, will and do; one who knows the self has nothing left to fret about. Know it while you are here, he says, don't brood over many words, and live calm and collected.
prasang.lesson: You become what you desire and do; know what matters while you are here.

verse.meaning: Yajnavalkya is still speaking to King Janaka, who has come to ask what happens when a person dies. Yajnavalkya says that in the end, a person becomes what they desire, will, and do. If they have known the self, they become immortal. If not, they go to sorrow. He tells the king to know this truth while he is still here, not to get lost in many words, and to live calm and collected.
verse.for_you: All these changes are pulling you in every direction at once, and you are trying to decide what comes next before you have even settled into the next room. The texts say you become what you do.
verse.try_today: Notice what you are actually doing right now, not what you could be doing.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: King Dhritarashtra cannot sleep the night before the peace talks. He calls his half-brother Vidura, who tells him how a wise person acts. One who decides and then begins does not stop halfway or waste time. They keep themselves in hand. This is the mark of wisdom. The fool, by contrast, is restless, caught in worry and delay. The wise person chooses action calmly, forgives freely, and knows what real happiness is made of.
verse.for_you: You are in the middle of a big shift and the question of staying or leaving is still open. That is exactly where Vidura's wise person stands. They decide, then begin. Their mind is not scattered by the change. They keep themselves in hand, steady through the uncertainty.
verse.try_today: Pick one small task for work and finish it completely, without checking anything else.
asks: How do I decide when the future is still a blur?
What does it mean to keep myself in hand right now?
How do I know if I am being wise or just avoiding the hard choice?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
verse.line: Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.
verse.translation: One joined to this understanding casts off both good and bad results here. So devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen, unwilling to act. Krishna tells him that one who understands the nature of action cuts through the chains of success and failure. The teaching is that yoga is skill in action. It means doing the work with your full attention, without letting the result own you. The work is the point, not the prize it might bring.
verse.for_you: You are standing at a fork in your career, and the weight of the outcome is keeping you still. The skill is not in choosing the perfect path right now. It is in taking the next step with your full attention. Let the result go.
verse.try_today: Pick one small task at work and do it with your full focus. Let go of the result.
verse.scene_line: You are on the edge of a choice, with the whole future waiting to be decided.
asks: How do I let go of the result when the result feels so big?
Can I start before I know how it will end?

story.title: Vibhishan crosses over
story.story_hook: Vibhishan arrived at the enemy camp with nothing but his name.
story.summary: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.
story.lesson: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.

anchor.speaker: Ram
anchor.setting: Ram, when Sugriva suspects Vibhishan is a spy and urges him to be turned away.
anchor.sanskrit: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥
anchor.line: Deceit and tricks win nothing lasting. People with a clean mind are the ones who are trusted.
anchor.translation: "A person with a clean mind reaches me; I have no liking for deceit, tricks or fault-finding. Even if Ravana sent him to learn our secrets, there is no fear or loss in it for us, Sugriva."
anchor.why: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.

He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.
prasang.story_hook: Vibhishan arrived at the enemy camp with nothing but his name.

story.hook_title: Vibhishan walked into the enemy camp with nothing but his name
story.teaser: Vibhishan walked into the enemy camp with nothing but his name
story.for_you: Vibhishan left a place that was not safe and crossed a wide sea to find Ram. Ram did not wait to see what Vibhishan could give him. He opened his arms because the heart that crossed was clean. You are standing at your own edge right now.
asks: What is the one thing I am holding that I do not need to carry across?
Who or what is my sea right now?
